title: Briefing demo
goal: Understand the interaction and choose whether this pacing feels useful

chunks.title: One idea at a time
chunks.purpose: Start with the core interaction rather than the entire design.
chunks.mainPoint: A briefing presents one meaningful concept at a time while keeping the goal and prior context available.
keyPoints: Use Next and Back to control pace.
The Outline lists every section, so you can jump ahead or back at any time.
chunks.details:
Rich content can clarify a chunk without changing the authoring model.

| Content | Useful when |
|---|---|
| Tables | Evidence or tradeoffs are easier to compare in rows |
| Mermaid | A flow, architecture, or state transition is easier to see than read |
| Vega-Lite | A compact chart explains relative magnitude or trend |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  agent[Agent reasoning] --> briefing[Browser briefing]
  briefing --> feedback[Notes, comments and answers]
  feedback --> agent
```
remember: The interface controls presentation; the agent still does the research and reasoning.

questions.question: Which reading mode should a briefing open in?
questions.context: Decided here because it only concerns the pacing described above.

options.label: Paced, one chunk per screen
options.description: Open in the step-by-step view; the Outline lists every section.
tradeoffs: Skimming means jumping through the Outline

options.label: All sections on one page
options.description: Show every section in one long page instead of pacing them.

questions.question: What feels different from reading a normal long chat response?

chunks.title: Return only useful signal
chunks.purpose: Avoid making the briefing itself create more information overload.
chunks.mainPoint: The agent receives your answers, notes, and inline comments - not a noisy transcript of every click. A question you skip goes back as unresolved, never as approval.
remember: A comment or a note is how you ask for a follow-up.

questions.question: Which of these should the agent always get back?
questions.context: Pick any that apply; they are independent.

questions.question: Is there anything else the agent should receive from the interface?

keyContext: The same tool runs inside Pi, Claude Code, and Codex.
The browser is the presentation layer; the agent remains in the terminal.
tray.runningSummary: Briefing = paced semantic cards + persistent context + optional questions.
openQuestions: When should the agent invoke it proactively?

questions.question: How should briefing be triggered by default?
questions.context: This only affects when the agent opens the browser presentation; normal concise answers remain available.

options.label: Always proactive
options.description: Let the agent open a briefing whenever an answer crosses a complexity threshold.

options.label: Explicit or clearly complex requests
options.description: Reserve proactive invocation for only the clearest complex cases, otherwise ask for it.
tradeoffs: Some useful cases may remain in normal chat
